findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: Could be read as intentional strictness on canonical form, but then gate and apply should fail too; the modes disagree.
findingDetails.case: A doc carries version: 01.2.0.0. verify exits 1 with mismatch:1.2.0.0!=01.2.0.0 (expected 01.2.0.0), while gate exits 0 and apply exits 0 leaving the value untouched.
findingDetails.claim: verifyVersion fails a version whose normalized tuple equals itself but whose raw string is non-canonical (leading zeros), and apply cannot normalize it.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Checked whether apply or --update normalizes; both short-circuit on raw equality. Checked whether the standard forbids leading zeros; its regex does not.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Would drop if the standard declared leading zeros invalid and all three modes rejected them consistently.
findingDetails.evidence: VERSION_RE allows leading zeros, normalize4 parses 01 to 1, verify compares tupleStr(normalize4(v)) against the raw derived string, and apply short-circuits on raw equality (skip-equal), so nothing normalizes the value.
evidenceRefs: probe: A verify=1 mismatch:1.2.0.0!=01.2.0.0 | A apply=0 leaves 01.2.0.0 | A gate=0 ok=1
findingDetails.recommendation: Compare tupleStr(existing) against tupleStr(normalize4(derivedStr)), and let apply rewrite a non-canonical-but-equal value.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Single comparison site in verifyVersion; applyVersion raw-equality check is its counterpart. No other mode compares tuples against raw strings.
findingDetails.title: verify rejects a leading-zero 4-part version that gate, apply and the format regex accept
findingDetails.userImpact: A hand-run verify fails on a doc every other mode accepts and does not repair; the failure text is self-contradictory.

findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: Could be deliberate leniency toward a stub key, but inserting a duplicate is not a safe repair for it.
findingDetails.case: A doc has version: with no value. bump --check reports NOT RAISED (next 1.0.0.0); bump inserts version: 1.0.0.0 before the closing fence, leaving the empty key, so the file carries version: and version: 1.0.0.0.
findingDetails.claim: An empty version value is treated as a missing key and bump synthesizes a second version key instead of reporting it as malformed.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: js-yaml duplicate-key behavior not executable in this checkout (package absent); impact phrased conditionally. Checked that the line-based gate still accepts the result, so nothing else catches it.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Would drop if js-yaml provably resolved the duplicate last-wins with no downstream loss AND the standard blessed the duplicate.
findingDetails.evidence: The version-line regex requires a non-empty value, so versionLineIdx stays -1; the malformed guard fires only when versionLineIdx !== -1; withEdition inserts instead of replacing. Probe showed versionLines ["version:", "version: 1.0.0.0"] after bump, and gate accepts the file via the first non-empty match.
evidenceRefs: probe: S8 check=1 NOT RAISED ... version none | S8b bump=0 versionLines=[version:, version: 1.0.0.0]
findingDetails.recommendation: Treat ^version:\s*$ as present-but-malformed (same error as 1.2), or replace that line in place instead of inserting a second key.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Any doc where the version key exists with an empty value reaches the same insert path; the earlier malformed rule already blocks non-empty invalid values, so this is the one malformed shape that slips past it.
findingDetails.title: A valueless version key is treated as missing; bump then writes a duplicate version line
findingDetails.userImpact: A duplicate mapping key is committed; the shared js-yaml-backed parser catches parse errors and returns an empty mapping, so consumers of parsed frontmatter can lose every field while the version gates still pass.

findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: Once unpaired the file is technically an add, and the new-doc rule keeps a valid version; if that is the intended policy the standard's table should state the threshold behavior explicitly.
findingDetails.case: A doc is moved with git mv and its body fully rewritten in the same commit. Git pairs it as delete+add (similarity below the default rename threshold), the add path sees a valid head version with no base blob, and bump --check exits 0 with no raise.
findingDetails.claim: When git cannot pair a move below the similarity threshold, the body change under the moved path is never considered for a raise.
findingDetails.confidence: medium-high on mechanism (reproduced), medium on intended policy
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Verified the R path is correct when pairing succeeds (clean rename: no raise; rename+body: raise on the new path), so only the pairing failure is the hole.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Would drop if the standard declared below-threshold rewrites as new documents.
findingDetails.evidence: changedDocs invokes git diff --cached --raw -z -M with default similarity; the add path continues when headVersion is valid and baseVersion is null. Probe: raw status not R, bump --check exit 0 on a moved+rewritten doc whose version stayed 1.2.0.0.
evidenceRefs: probe: rename+40-line rewrite -> raw status not R, bump --check status=0
standard:72 says the edition goes up whenever the body changes
findingDetails.recommendation: State the threshold behavior in the standard, or extend pairing when similarity misses (for example pair A with D by basename or carried version).
findingDetails.scopeProof: The same add path covers copies and any rename git declines to pair; changedDocs and the bump loop are the only consumers of the diff.
findingDetails.title: Rename below git's similarity threshold is an add; a rewritten body raises nothing
findingDetails.userImpact: A moved-and-rewritten doc can carry a body change without raising its edition; the pre-commit gate and the PR check both read the same diff and agree it is fine, so the miss is silent.

findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: Could be dismissed as an absurd file name, but the engine already hardens the read side against exactly this class with -z, so the report channel silently drops a guarantee the rest of the tool keeps.
findingDetails.case: A staged in-scope doc whose file name contains a newline has a body change and no version raise. bump rewrites the working-tree file and reports the raised path on stdout one line per path; the hook stages the split fragments, none of which is the real path, so the commit records the unraised blob.
findingDetails.claim: A raised path containing a newline never reaches the index, and the gate cannot see it because verification runs only on the split fragments.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Checked whether console.log escapes the newline (it does not) or a NUL-safe report exists (none; stdout is captured as text); checked whether the name-only pre-filter at pre-commit:845 would skip such a doc (it is a non-emptiness test only, so the engine still runs); checked whether verification covers the full set (per fragment only).
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: If the raised-path report moves to NUL-delimited output consumed NUL-safe, or staging verification diffs the full raised set instead of per-path fragments.
findingDetails.evidence: frontmatter-version.mjs:437 writes the raise; :439 prints the path with console.log. pre-commit:875 captures stdout as text; :898-904 iterates line-by-line; :900 git add -- "$DOCV_PATH" 2>/dev/null || true fails silently for fragments; :903 git diff --quiet -- "$DOCV_PATH" checks fragments only, so DOCV_LEFT stays empty and the gate passes.
findingDetails.recommendation: Emit raised paths NUL-delimited and read them with a NUL-safe loop, or verify staging against the complete raised set.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The stdout report is the only engine-to-hook channel for raised paths (only print site :439; only consumer pre-commit:898-904). changedDocs already treats paths as NUL-unsafe on the read side (:346), so the report side is the sole deviation.
findingDetails.title: A newline in a staged doc path silently skips the raise staging
findingDetails.userImpact: The pre-commit gate raise-and-stage contract is bypassed: a commit can carry a changed doc with the old version, and the working tree is left with an uncommitted raise. The PR job catches covered pull requests, but direct pushes to main or skilled/** carry it.

findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: Could be treated as out of scope because it needs local write access, but the code comment claims it only ever writes inside the skills root, and a symlink silently falsifies that claim at two write sites.
findingDetails.case: A worktree file at an in-scope doc path is a symlink to a target outside the skills root while the index holds regular doc content needing a raise. The only containment check compares path.resolve strings (symlink-blind) and the bump write has none, so fs.writeFileSync follows the link and rewrites the target.
findingDetails.claim: A symlinked worktree path passes lexical containment and the write follows it outside the skills tree.
findingDetails.confidence: medium (mechanism high; reachability requires local worktree tampering)
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: A staged symlink (mode 120000) carries the link target as its blob, parses as no frontmatter, and is skipped before any write, so the repository index alone cannot trigger it; the hook-trust block skips the toolchain for clones that do not share the checkout git common dir (pre-commit:33-56), so a hostile clone cannot run this code. The remaining route needs a worktree file replaced by a symlink while the index holds doc content - local tampering plus a commit.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: If write sites re-check fs.realpathSync containment or refuse symlinks via lstat, or the worktree is documented as fully trusted input.
findingDetails.evidence: applyVersion guard at :270 is path.resolve(absFile).startsWith(path.resolve(opts.skillsRoot) + path.sep); its write at :292 follows it. bumpDocs filters with lexical inScope (:174, :391), reads through the path in the partial guard (:429), and writes at :437 with no re-check. Roots are realpath-ed for comparison (:380-381); write targets are not.
findingDetails.recommendation: Resolve the write target with fs.realpathSync and compare containment on the real path, or skip paths whose lstat says symlink.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Every doc-content write in the engine is one of two sites (:292, :437); neither resolves symlinks before writing.
findingDetails.title: Symlinks defeat the containment checks; the bump write has no containment check at all
findingDetails.userImpact: A write the gate believes is confined to the skills tree can land on an arbitrary file the symlink points at, and the hook then git-adds the same path as if it were the doc.

findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: Running checks from the change under review is universal; the finding is specifically that this job is a gate whose truth depends on code its subjects control, with no integrity anchor, while the adjacent job demonstrates the repository counter-pattern.
findingDetails.case: A pull request edits frontmatter-version.mjs so bump --check exits 0 while also carrying docs whose versions did not go up. The job checks out the PR ref (no base ref override) and runs that edited engine, so the check passes on exactly the change it exists to catch.
findingDetails.claim: The enforcing code is loaded from the untrusted change under test, so the check can be neutered by the same PR it evaluates.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Checked for a ref/hash pin of the engine (none), a second check from main (none), and whether the pre-commit gate backstops (it runs a committer-controlled engine too, and ordinary commits are its bypass surface).
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: If the job runs the engine from a base-ref copy or hash, or a separate required check verifies engine integrity against main.
findingDetails.evidence: Job is pull_request-only (workflow:52), checks out the PR ref with no ref pin (:56-58), installs and builds from that checkout (:66-71), and runs node .skilled/skills/sk-doc/shared/scripts/frontmatter-version.mjs bump --check (:78). The sibling coverage job fails closed when its guard file is missing (:34-40); the version job has no pin, hash, or base copy of the engine.
evidenceRefs: .github/workflows/skill-doc-frontmatter.yml:66-71 npm ci + tsc build from the checkout
findingDetails.recommendation: Run the check with the engine loaded from the base ref, or add a required integrity check on the engine file.
findingDetails.scopeProof: One job runs the check; nothing else in CI re-runs the engine from a trusted ref.
findingDetails.title: The CI version check executes the pull request's own engine
findingDetails.userImpact: False assurance: a green result does not prove the version invariant when the PR touches the engine, so that invariant depends on reviewer attention for exactly those PRs.
